_about: The composition ladder: the same 1,080 scenarios asked as pairs, as triples, and as the one five-way set.

WHAT IT IS FOR. Every run so far has sent pairs, and the study's headline is whether pairwise measurements PREDICT what happens when three or five sources compete. `python3 -m ipb.stats.phase1` shows exactly why that cannot be answered from pairs: two worlds with identical pairwise win rates can have a different three-way winner. This is the run that collects the other half.

THE SIZES ARE THE DECLARED LADDER. dataset-plan.md declares n = 2, 3, 5 and data/splits/set.json freezes which sets stage one fits and which it predicts. Four-way sets are enumerated there under `not_in_declared_ladder` and are deliberately not sent.

REFUSAL IS NOT IN IT ABOVE A PAIR, and that is the plan working. A composition of n sources needs n mutually exclusive options; refusal has two, comply and decline, because it is binary by nature. dataset-plan.md has said since it was written that refusal is pairwise only, never pooled into the main scale. So sizes 3 and 5 carry 960 scenarios, not 1,080, and the runner says so when it builds the list.

NO SOLO ARM, ON PURPOSE. Solo ability is a property of (scenario, option) and `balanced-qwen3-14b` already measured it for the pairs on this model. Adding size 1 here would emit ten more solo trials per scenario and quadruple the run; add it in a separate run if the triples turn out to need their own control.

COST. 3,000 trials at 3 draws each is 9,000 draws -- the same size as balanced-qwen3-14b, which took about two and a half hours on two cards. Check before you start: scripts/run_trials.sh prints the plan, and `python3 -m ipb.runner.design ladder-qwen3-14b --balance` shows what it sends and how evenly.
seed: base_seed differs from every other run, so a draw is a draw and not the same draw sent twice.
Read it with scripts/analyse.sh, then `scripts/strengths.sh ladder-qwen3-14b` for the fit -- which, for the first time, will have a composition above a pair to predict.
